title: Your RC1 review, pages 1 to 9: seven rules, six tasks, and the team back on nights
headline: Four batches in (pages 1 to 9 and one task), each kept in your words and mapped to chapter and text. They add up to seven rules for the whole book, not only the pages you marked. The team is back to round the clock while it has work, and every wake now uses its full time. The work is already routed: the storyteller (the walkthrough), the researcher (your articles and the graph), the publisher and designer (layout, the page 9 gap, QR codes), ruv.sgit and the designer (experiments in the chapters).

sections.title: The seven rules, as I read them

head: Rule
From
rows: Punchlines first, logistics last: open with what was achieved, the idea, a visual
The record is a side effect of how the team works (determinism, provenance, memory); never 'captured'
The talk was not finished; the brakes analogy is a start (many technologies let a car go fast; we trust brakes because we use them)
Visuals big, and experimented in the chapters themselves; the best of the slides, not all
Ask of every page what it is trying to say; cut what does not serve it
The book teaches the reader to replicate the workflow: prompts, steps, QR codes; the reader ends where you began
Footnotes, links and QR codes to your articles: the augmented book, with a graph of references

sections.title: Page 9: why nobody caught the image
sections.text: The infographics were placed at the last build step, outside the chapter files every member reviews, and nothing in the workflow looks at the printed pages: the gate checks the site's HTML. Now: the publisher adds a check that reports every oversized image at each build, and the designer looks at every printed page of every build (task A2).

ruv.sgit and designer: T4, experiments in the chapters, page 8's animation first
conductor: A1, other agents on the team, a study when you have finished the review
